Dispatched gpt-6.1-sol effort high; PGID 1867806
Fresh full review of PR #643 at exact head 31a26154c59089c9400dc19af0faffec631f1d66. Profile: semantic-system within rules-clause-complete.

Scope and authority: reviewed the complete origin/main...HEAD diff (all nine changed files), the single origin/main..HEAD commit, the entire new inventory, the v2 ledger/report/presentation consumers, tool registration and implementation boundaries, curated engine producers/consumers, permanent evidence, and relevant records.json and vendored SRD PDF text. Read AGENTS.md, docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (including From observation to finding and Findings discipline), docs/importer-fix-protocol.md, ADR 0020, the current owning and review beads, dispatch .4, historical children .1/.2/.3, and disclosed follow-ups .13 and eshyra-4xx6. The refs/beads/state projection is stale against live Beads; current live DESIGN/acceptance criteria and ADR 0020 govern, not the superseded bootstrap/global-closure notes.

The bounded registry accounts for 74 tools as 71 tool entries plus three named non-capabilities, alongside 15 curated engine entries. The four ledger contracts are referenced rather than independently restated; the magic-item backlog remains an unselected candidate report. resolve-check-v2 correctly incorporates sheet-derived ability/proficiency behavior, and its six existing rule bindings move together without adding presentation bindings. These structural properties do not prove semantic truthfulness of the other entries.

Verification: repository clean and exact HEAD reconfirmed; no repository files edited or created, no formatting/install/build/verification mutation, no GitHub writes, commits, or pushes. Vitest dependencies are absent in this worktree, so no test suite was executed; cited test assertions were inspected as committed evidence, not claimed as fresh passes.

S1 — BLOCKING: selected character usage economies are falsely declared DM-supplied.
Invariant/authority: every W13 operation, exclusion, and residual interpretation must describe the existing implementation truthfully (owning DESIGN D1/D2 and acceptance criteria; ADR 0020 section 3).
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1063 and :1067.
Concrete scenario: a sheet-backed level-3 barbarian's first spend_usage of Rage derives maximum/reset from the active class table and succeeds without maxUses/reset. Following the inventory's instruction to declare them is refused. usageCounters.ts:882 selects the bound-resource path before the legacy declaration path; :977 explicitly rejects the declared economy.
Sibling analysis: checked Rage/rages, Ki/ki-points, Sorcery Points/font-of-magic, active-pack overrides and stale/alias reconciliation, unavailable and unlimited capacities, and restore/reset/rest consumers. Characters without a matching sheet/class-resource binding and unbound item charges really do use the declaration path. The separate class-resource-capacity-v1 entry does not cure the contradictory spend_usage statement.
Closure: state the selected pack-bound character resource branch and its refusal of declared capacity, limit DM-supplied economies to genuinely unbound abilities/items, and reconcile operation/exclusions/residual interpretation with the existing class-resource entry. Do not change runtime behavior.
Permanent evidence: generalized active-capacity and usage-accounting invariants already protected by classResourceActiveCapacity.test.ts and usageCounters.test.ts, both existing pointers; retain that evidence and accurately connect it to the corrected contract. New per-tool behavioral suites are not required.
Repair material: YES, the authoritative resource-ownership meaning changes.

S2 — BLOCKING: remove_effect_target promises lifecycle continuity and idempotency that cleanup cascades invalidate.
Invariant/authority: truthful lifecycle/state-integrity boundaries and refusals (owning D2 and acceptance criteria; ADR 0020 section 3).
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:508, :511, :512.
Concrete scenario: the existing activeEffects.test.ts:4548 constructs A concentrated by goblin 1 owning/targeting goblin 2, and B concentrated by goblin 2 owning goblin 1. Removing goblin 2 from A triggers owned-creature cleanup, breaks B, removes A's owner, and ends A. The result explicitly reports superseded:true and effect.status:ended. A retry is refused by activeEffects.ts:5154, rather than the advertised unconditional no-op. The engine implements cascade supersession at :5249/:5293/:5326.
Sibling analysis: checked direct end, partial target cleanup, repeated same/different reason, terminal guards, creation supersession, expiry and combat-closure cycles. Ordinary removal preserves the effect only when cleanup does not supersede it; same-reason retry is a no-op only while the effect has not ended.
Closure: qualify continuity and retry claims, describe owned-creature cleanup's possible terminal cascade and superseded result, and point to the committed activeEffects evidence rather than implying end_effect is the only route to ending an effect. Preserve existing runtime behavior and terminal-event integrity.
Permanent evidence: generalized cascade/terminal-event invariant in the existing re-entrant cleanup group of activeEffects.test.ts, with an exact committed example at :4548. Reference that evidence; no new near-identical reproducer is needed.
Repair material: YES, the authoritative lifecycle guarantee changes.

S3 — BLOCKING: combat lifecycle entries erase operative participant and transition distinctions.
Invariant/authority: capability refusals must be stated for the actual admitted participant/transition, not generalized from one branch (owning D2 and acceptance criteria; ADR 0020 section 3).
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:600 and :642.
Concrete scenarios: (a) an opted-in player-character combatant above 0 HP accepts status:'stable' together with damage reducing it to 0 as a knockout; encounterCombatants.ts:3877/:3908 implement this, and encounterCombatants.test.ts:1803 asserts successful knockout even with a large damage delta. The inventory instead says explicit stable is refused. (b) begin_turn for a stable party character with no due recovery/effect transition returns turnAvailable:true: actionEconomy.ts:611 treats only dead characters as unavailable, whereas :588 additionally treats stable/escaped/inactive/absent combatants as unavailable. :948 derives the returned flag from that type-specific boundary. The inventory falsely applies the combatant status set to every participant.
Sibling analysis: varied monster versus player-character death rules, positive-to-zero versus already-zero HP, dying versus stable, zero-HP vanish/revert rules, party characters versus combatants, and boundary transitions. Explicit dying remains refused; stable without a knockout transition remains refused; dying participants retain death-save turns; dead characters are unavailable. Checked adjacent HP/death-save/stabilization and turn-resource entries against their owners.
Closure: state the stable knockout exception and preserve the separate character/combatant begin-turn guards, including assessment after boundary settlement. Represent any remaining adjudication without claiming a code guard the engine lacks. This is a correction of inventory metadata, not authorization to change lifecycle behavior.
Permanent evidence: generalized lifecycle/participant-boundary evidence in encounterCombatants.test.ts, actionEconomy.test.ts and the existing lifecycle tests; retain/reference it with accurate contract distinctions. No new per-tool behavioral suite is required.
Repair material: YES, authoritative supported/refused inputs and turn availability change.

S4 — BLOCKING: set_surprised advertises a side-identity guard it does not implement.
Invariant/authority: a declared deterministic refusal must exist at the real admission boundary (owning D2 and acceptance criteria; ADR 0020 section 3). The source rule compares hiders against opposing creatures (rule:surprise, SRD PDF p.90); that source responsibility must not be misrepresented as an engine-enforced side guard.
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:679.
Concrete scenario: active retained checks from hiders on opposing sides, each compared against the same identified observer set, pass this tool's checks. With noticed:true comparisons it returns success with surprised:[] at toolSetSurprised.ts:166. Its query at :52 does not even read hider participant identity or sides; :144 only rejects unequal observer sets. Consequently mixed sides are not categorically refused as claimed.
Sibling analysis: checked duplicate IDs/pairs, missing or stale checks, observer identity/membership, same versus mismatched observer sets, all-noticed versus not-noticed observers, and the downstream first-turn surprise guard. retainedChecks.test.ts:315 protects mismatched-set refusal, not a side-identity refusal; downstream setSurprisedInTransaction receives observers only and cannot repair this claim.
Closure: name the actual mismatched-observer-set guard and leave selecting opposing hiders/observers with the DM; remove the unconditional mixed-side refusal claim. No new engine capability or runtime side validation is authorized by this bead.
Permanent evidence: generalized retained-comparison and first-turn invariants in the existing retainedChecks.test.ts and actionEconomy.test.ts. Use their real guard claims in the inventory; no dedicated new side-validation behavior test is required.
Repair material: YES, the authoritative fail-closed boundary changes.

S5 — BLOCKING: creation contracts credit a requirements calculator with selection validation and declare inputs for the wrong callable boundary.
Invariant/authority: operation, required inputs, and module/entryPoint identity must describe the same real capability (owning D1/D2 and acceptance criteria; ADR 0020 section 3).
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1387–1399; sibling :1365.
Concrete scenario: level1SpellRequirements accepts a resolved class record, ability modifiers, and a resolver (creationSpellCounts.ts:40), and computes numeric requirements. It accepts no chosen spell list and cannot classify selections, exclude chosen always-prepared spells, or gate a deficient wizard spellbook. Its result is the same whether a draft has five or six starting wizard spells. The actual classification, always-prepared exclusion, count validation and diagnostics are in characterDraft.ts:1168 onward, and finalization consumes those diagnostics via the draft engine. A draft plus resolver, the advertised inputs, is not this function's signature; omitting ability modifiers also omits a required preparation-limit dependency.
Sibling analysis: checked known-caster counts, wizard spellbook/prepared-list membership and count, cleric/druid preparation with subclass always-prepared spells, and finalizeCharacterDraft's actual gate. deriveCreationClassChoices similarly receives resolved class data, stored choices, held skill/tool proficiencies and resolver (creationClassChoices.ts:90/:118), not a draft directly; those proficiencies govern validation. Other curated engine identities were checked against their implementations; this finding does not demand one entry per helper.
Closure: describe the requirements calculator with its real inputs and limits, and locate the existing draft validation/gating responsibility at its actual owner, without duplicating or losing the finalized-creation commitment. Reconcile the class-choice input description with its actual resolved inputs and proficiency-dependent validation. Do not implement new creation behavior.
Permanent evidence: generalized creation count/selection and choice-validation invariants already in creationSpellCounts.test.ts, creationClassChoices.test.ts and finalizeCharacter.test.ts; retain/reference those existing tests and accurately name their runtime owners. A new behavioral suite is not required.
Repair material: YES, the authoritative operation/input/owner boundaries change.

S6 — BLOCKING: the inventory omits existing advancement decisions and award operations from its in-force set.
Invariant/authority: one inventory must enumerate every in-force deterministic operation (owning acceptance criteria and October 9 rebaseline: enumerate from tool registrations AND pack-consuming paths). D3's exclusion of engine-code closure is a limit on proof claims, not permission to omit an identified selected operation. docs/design/character-progression.md expressly assigns eligibility and auditable advancement totals to deterministic core; ADR 0020 section 3 preserves those commitments.
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1324 (ENGINE_PATHS), :1431 onward (level-up entry), and :1677 onward (progression-event entry); particularly :1693.
Concrete scenario: a level-1 XP-mode character at 300 XP deterministically becomes eligible for level 2 through getLevelUpEligibility (levelUpEligibility.ts:95; levelUpEligibility.test.ts:76; table:character-advancement and SRD PDF p.56). The real CLI playProgression.ts:28 and guidedLevelUpFlow.ts:100 consume that decision. No inventory operation describes it: applyLevelUp explicitly excludes deciding eligibility/awarding XP, and recordProgressionEvent explicitly says storage only with no eligibility. Likewise awardXp atomically changes XP and appends the matching audit event under XP-mode/positive-amount guards (domainMutations.ts:1223), and grantMilestone checks milestone policy before appending its award (:1291); neither is represented by the generic field mutation or storage operation.
Sibling analysis: checked XP thresholds and multi-level catch-up, already-consumed advancement, outstanding milestone counting, opposite-mode award refusals, atomic award plus ledger writes, separate applyLevelUp, and raw ledger storage. Merely listing levelUpEligibility.ts/advancementPolicy.ts as runtimeOwner does not enumerate their distinct operation. The bounded omitted set is advancement eligibility and policy-guarded XP/milestone awards; this is not a demand for global engine/SRD closure or a symbol census.
Closure: add truthful W13 contracts for these already-selected progression responsibilities (or explicitly incorporate them into correctly identified, non-duplicated capability boundaries), with inputs, guards, residual DM award decisions, owners and existing evidence. Reconcile engine-capability-ownership's accepted reasoning after the in-force scope and truthfulness defects are repaired; do not add new model-facing bindings or runtime capabilities.
Permanent evidence: generalized eligibility and atomic/mode-constrained award invariants already in levelUpEligibility.test.ts and progressionAwards.test.ts, together with guidedLevelUpFlow.test.ts. Reference those; no universal engine closure test or new per-helper tests are required.
Repair material: YES, the authoritative inventory's semantic membership expands to cover omitted existing responsibilities.

NOT A FINDING — no requirement for global deterministic engine/SRD closure, zero engine-pending clauses, or converting the unselected magic-item backlog into implemented capabilities.
NOT A FINDING — no requirement for new per-tool behavioral suites; D3's bounded closure/path evidence and existing behavior evidence are the authorized proof burden.
NOT A FINDING — no requirement that staged executor kinds have current consumers to be retained; staged responsibility, successor eshyra-4xx6 and next integration state are named.
NOT A FINDING — the pre-move test literals' v1-to-v2 update is authorized by D2/D5's truthfulness correction; binding membership and source-fidelity protection are preserved.
NOT A FINDING — existing caller-declared roll/economy risks disclosed in .13 do not themselves falsify the inventory's explicitly limited contracts; runtime redesign is outside this bead.
NOT A FINDING — no requirement for deep freezing every metadata array or treating malformed diagnostic backlog input as a new product schema gate.

All six blockers belong to the owning inventory repair; none is deferred as a minor follow-up. Owning bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 was not modified or closed.
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED (6)
